source.title: SOME OF MY FAVORITE OPEN PROBLEMS

accepted.question_text: Let Ω be the unit ball in R³ and consider the Dirichlet problem -Δu = u⁵ + λu in Ω with u = 0 on ∂Ω, where u is sought as a smooth real-valued function and λ is a parameter. If 0 < λ ≤ λ₁/4, where λ₁ = π² is the first Dirichlet eigenvalue of -Δ on Ω, does this problem admit a nontrivial solution u ≢ 0?
accepted.context_brief: Critical elliptic equation in 3D

evidence.quote:
Open Problem 1.1 (implicit in ([BrNi1]). Assume that
(1.2) 0 < λ≤ λ1/4.
Does there exist a solution u̸≡ 0 of (1.1)?

accepted.question_text: Let Ω be the unit disc in R² and let u:Ω→R² solve the Ginzburg-Landau system -Δu = (1/ε²)u(1-|u|²) in Ω with boundary condition u(x)=x on ∂Ω. Writing Uε for the standard radial solution x/|x|·fε(|x|), is Uε the unique solution of this boundary value problem for each ε>0?
accepted.context_brief: Uniqueness for Ginzburg-Landau vortex

evidence.quote:
Open Problem 2.1 ([BBH, Problem 10 in Chapter XI]). Is the radial
solution Uε the only solution of (2.1)?

accepted.question_text: In the same unit-disc Ginzburg-Landau setting, let Eε(u)= (1/2)∫Ω|∇u|² + (1/(4ε²))∫Ω(|u|²-1)² on H¹_g(Ω;R²) with boundary datum g(x)=x on ∂Ω. Is the radial solution Uε a global minimizer of Eε on H¹_g(Ω;R²) for every ε>0?
accepted.context_brief: Variational minimality of radial Ginzburg-Landau solution

evidence.quote:
Open Problem 2.2. Is Uε a minimizer of Eε on H1
g (Ω; R2) for any ε > 0?

accepted.question_text: For p>2, consider the p-Ginzburg-Landau energy Eε,p(u)= (1/p)∫Ω|∇u|ᵖ + (1/(4ε²))∫Ω(|u|²-1)² on the unit disc Ω⊂R² with boundary condition u(x)=x on ∂Ω. If uε is any minimizer, or more generally any critical point, does uε(x) converge to x/|x| on Ω\{0} as ε→0?
accepted.context_brief: Asymptotic radial symmetry for p-Ginzburg-Landau

evidence.quote:

any minimizer (resp. critical point) of Eε,p on W 1,p
g (Ω, R2). Does uε(x)→ x/|x|
in Ω\{ 0} as ε→ 0?

accepted.question_text: Consider entire smooth solutions u:R²→R²≃C of -Δu = u(1-|u|²) on R² such that |u(x)|→1 as |x|→∞, so the degree at infinity q=deg(u,∞) is well defined. Must every such solution coincide, up to a translation x↦x-x₀ and multiplication by a unit complex number α, with the standard radial degree-q solution V_q?
accepted.context_brief: Classification of entire Ginzburg-Landau solutions

evidence.quote:
Open Problem 2.4 ([BBH, Problem 14], [BMR], [Br3]). Let u be any
solution of (2.5) - (2.6). Does u coincide with Vq modulo rotation and translation,
where q = deg( u,∞)? I.e., is u(x) = αVq(x− x0) for some α∈ C,|α| = 1, and
x0∈ R2?

accepted.question_text: If u:R²→R² is a smooth solution of -Δu = u(1-|u|²) on R² with |u(x)|→1 as |x|→∞, must the potential energy defect be integrable, meaning ∫R²(|u|²-1)² < ∞?
accepted.context_brief: Energy integrability for entire Ginzburg-Landau solutions

evidence.quote:
Open Problem 2.5 ([BMR, Problem 2], [Br3, Open Problem 2]). Assume
that u satisﬁes (2.5) and (2.6). Does (2.11) hold?

accepted.question_text: Let Ω be the unit disc in R² and consider smooth harmonic maps u:Ω→S² satisfying -Δu_i = u_i|∇u|² for i=1,2,3, together with boundary data g(x,y)=(Rx,Ry,√(1-R²)) on ∂Ω for some 0<R<1. Besides the two explicit solutions u and ū written in formulas (3.7) and (3.8), are there any other solutions of this boundary value problem?
accepted.context_brief: Additional harmonic maps from disc to sphere

evidence.quote:
Open Problem 3.1 ([BrCo]). Assume g is given by (3.6). Are there other
solutions of (3.1)-(3.3) besides u and ¯u?

accepted.question_text: Let Ω=B³ be the unit ball in R³ and let g:∂Ω≃S²→S² be smooth with degree zero. Does there exist a continuous map u:Ω̄→S² that is harmonic in Ω, satisfies -Δu_i = u_i|∇u|² for i=1,2,3, has |u|=1 in Ω, and obeys the boundary condition u=g on ∂Ω?
accepted.context_brief: Continuous harmonic maps with degree-zero boundary data

evidence.quote:
Open Problem 4.1 ([HaLi], [Ha], [Br5, Open Problem 3]). Assume that
(4.6) holds. Does there exist a continuous harmonic map satisfying (4.1)-(4.3)?

accepted.question_text: In the same B³→S² setting with degree-zero boundary data g, consider the variational problem of minimizing the Dirichlet energy E(u)=∫Ω|∇u|² over the class H¹_g(Ω;S²)∩C(Ω̄). Is the infimum of this constrained energy among continuous competitors actually attained by some continuous map?
accepted.context_brief: Attainment of continuous harmonic-map infimum

accepted.question_text: Define the relaxed energy R on H¹_g(Ω;S²) by taking the lower semicontinuous relaxation of the Dirichlet energy with respect to weak H¹ limits of continuous S²-valued maps, and consider minimizers of Min{R(u): u∈H¹_g(Ω;S²)}. Must every minimizer of this relaxed problem be continuous on Ω̄, or at least is there always at least one continuous minimizer?
accepted.context_brief: Continuity of relaxed-energy minimizers

evidence.quote:
Open Problem 4.3 ([BBC]). Are the minimizers of (4.10) continuous on ¯Ω? (Is
it true for at least one of the minimizers?)

accepted.question_text: Let u be a minimizer of the relaxed-energy problem Min{R(u):u∈H¹_g(Ω;S²)}, where R(u)=∫Ω|∇u|²+S(u) and J_u=(1/3)div D(u) is the associated distributional Jacobian. Must S(u)=0, equivalently J_u=0, or equivalently can every such minimizer be approximated strongly in H¹ by continuous maps u_n∈H¹_g(Ω;S²)∩C(Ω̄)?
accepted.context_brief: Vanishing singular part for relaxed-energy minimizers

accepted.question_text: For continuous maps f:S¹→S¹, Theorem 5.2 gives an estimate |deg f| ≤ C ∬ [|f(x)-f(y)|≥√3]/|x-y|². Is there a simpler and more geometric proof of this theorem? What is the optimal constant C in that inequality, and is the optimal constant attained?

accepted.question_text: For 1<p<∞ and integer d, let m_{p,d} be the infimum of the W^{1/p,p}-seminorm energy among maps f:S¹→S¹ of degree d. Is m_{p,d}=|d|·m_{p,1} for every d∈Z, and is the infimum defining m_{p,d} always achieved?
accepted.context_brief: Exact energy of degree-d classes

(5.15) mp,d =|d|mp,1 ∀d∈ Z?

accepted.question_text: Suppose f,g:S¹→S¹ have identical Fourier-modulus data |a_n(f)|=|a_n(g)| for every n∈Z. Does the positive conclusion of Theorem 5.5, namely deg f = deg g, remain valid when f and g lie only in the larger classes W^{1/p,p}(S¹;S¹) with p>3 or C^{0,α}(S¹;S¹) with α≤1/3? The problem is open even in mixed-regularity cases such as f∈W^{1/p,p} with 2<p≤3 and g∈W^{1/q,q} with q>3, or f∈C^{0,α} with α>1/3 and g∈C^{0,β} with β≤1/3.
accepted.context_brief: Can one hear the degree beyond the 1/3 threshold?

evidence.quote:
Open Problem 5.5. What happens to Theorem 5.5 when f, g∈ W 1/p,p(S1; S1)
with p > 3 (resp. f, g∈ C0,α(S1 : S1) with α≤ 1/3)? The problem is open even
under the stronger assumption that f∈ W 1/p,p with 2 < p ≤ 3 and g∈ W 1/q,q
with q > 3 (resp. f∈ C0,α with α > 1/3 and g∈ C0,β with β≤ 1/3).

accepted.question_text: A summation process is a family (σ_{n,ε})_{n∈Z,0<ε<1} such that for each ε, sup_n |n||σ_{n,ε}|<∞ and for each fixed n, σ_{n,ε}→1 as ε→0. For any p>3, or for Hölder regularity exponent α≤1/3, does there exist a summation process depending only on p (respectively only on α) such that lim_{ε→0} Σ_{n∈Z} n|a_n(f)|²σ_{n,ε} = deg f for every f in W^{1/p,p}(S¹;S¹) (respectively every f in C^{0,α}(S¹;S¹))?
accepted.context_brief: Universal summation processes for degree recovery

accepted.question_text: Given an individual map f∈C(S¹;S¹), or more generally f∈VMO(S¹;S¹), does there always exist some summation process (σ_{n,ε}) depending on that particular f such that lim_{ε→0} Σ_{n∈Z} n|a_n(f)|²σ_{n,ε} equals deg f?

accepted.question_text: Let B be the closed unit ball in Rᴺ and let f:B→B be a VMO map. Must it be true that for every ε>0 the set {x∈B : |f(x)-x|<ε} has positive measure?
accepted.context_brief: Brouwer-type fixed-point property for VMO maps

evidence.quote:
Open Problem 5.10. Let B be the closed unit ball in RN and let f be a VMO
map from B into itself. Is it true that for every ε > 0, the set
{x∈ B;|f(x)− x| < ε}
has positive measure?

accepted.question_text: Consider the extremal solution u* associated with -Δu = λf(u) in a smooth bounded convex domain Ω⊂Rᴺ, with u>0 in Ω, u=0 on ∂Ω, and f(u)=eᵘ. When N≥10, must u* be unbounded? If some convex domains give a bounded extremal solution for f(u)=eᵘ, can one instead find another increasing convex nonlinearity f satisfying the stated hypotheses for which u* is unbounded on that domain?
accepted.context_brief: Unbounded extremal solutions in high dimensions

evidence.quote:
Open Problem 6.1 ([BrVa], [Br6]). Assume Ω is a bounded smooth convex
set in RN , N≥ 10. Let f(u) = eu. Is u∗ unbounded? If the answer is negative
for some domains Ω, can one ﬁnd other functions f satisfying (6.2)-(6.3) (possibly
depending on Ω) such that u∗ /∈ L∞(Ω)?

accepted.question_text: Assume the extremal solution u* of the semilinear Dirichlet problem is unbounded. What can be said about its blow-up set, and in particular, if Ω is convex, must that blow-up set reduce to a single point?
accepted.context_brief: Geometry of blow-up sets for extremal solutions

evidence.quote:
Open Problem 6.2 ([BrVa], [Br6]). Assume u∗ /∈ L∞(Ω). What can be said
about the blow-up set of u∗? Does it consist of a single point when Ω is convex?

accepted.question_text: For functions ψ on the torus, does the Bourgain-Brezis-type estimate ||ψ-∫ψ||_{H^{1/2}+W^{1,1}} ≤ C ||∇ψ||_{H^{-1/2}+L¹} hold universally?
accepted.context_brief: Missing Bourgain-Brezis estimate

evidence.quote: Open Problem 7.1 ([BoBr]). Does (7.9) hold?

accepted.question_text: Let Ω be a smooth bounded domain in Rᴺ, N≥2, and let U be the unique minimizer of Φ(u)=∫Ω|∇u| + (1/2)∫Ω|u-f|² over BV(Ω)∩L²(Ω), where f is smooth on Ω̄. Is the distributional gradient ∇U itself a BV function on Ω?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 8.1 ([Br10, Open Problem 1]). Does∇U belong to BV (Ω)?

accepted.question_text: Let Q be the unit cube in Rᴺ and define f_N(t)=inf{P(S): S⊂Q measurable, |S|=t}, where P(S) is the relative perimeter inside Q. For N≥3, is there an explicit formula analogous to the two-dimensional formula f₂(t), and in particular is it true that f_N(t)≡1 for t near 1/2?
accepted.context_brief: Sharp relative isoperimetric profile of the cube
